spec.title: 🌍 Global OSINT Map
spec.description: Section header for the geographic map below.

spec.title: Malicious JA4 Hits
spec.description: Number of network connections whose TLS Client Hello fingerprint (JA4+) matched a known-malicious signature database (e.g. known RAT/C2 frameworks like AsyncRAT or Cobalt Strike). Any non-zero value here is high-confidence — JA4+ collisions with legitimate software are rare, so treat spikes as urgent.

spec.title: 📜 All Evaluated Alerts (Live Stream, whole network)
spec.description: Every candidate alert across the whole network, published or not, with the decision and the false-positive engine's call. Use it to spot patterns across devices, e.g. several devices hitting the same domain. Read the columns like this: 'decision' is the Argus engine's reasoning path (hypothesis_high, hard_stop and similar mean it reached HIGH/CRITICAL). 'fp_verdict' is only the false-positive filter's opinion: CONFIRMED_THREAT there means 'not judged a false positive', NOT 'confirmed attack'. The previous version filtered on a removed 'verdict' field, so it had been empty.

spec.expr: {job="home_ids_alerts"} | json | type="ids_alert" | json host="device.hostname", ip="device.ip", signature="signature", risk="risk", decision="hee_decision_path", fp_stage="fp_verdict.stage", fp_verdict="fp_verdict.verdict", fp_confidence="fp_verdict.confidence", domain="network_context.queried_domain", dest_ip="network_context.destination_ip"

spec.title: Network Geographic Footprint
spec.description: Plots every external IP Home-IDS has seen, colored/sized by home_ids_geo_country_marker (same risk value as home_ids_geo_risk, paired with a static per-country centroid so the map has coordinates to plot -- see core/country_centroids.py). This metric is ONLY EVER SET once a connection's risk crosses alert_threshold=6.0 (metrics_sync.py) -- a country either doesn't appear on this map at all (benign), or already scores at least ~6 the moment it does. 6-8.99 = orange (crossed the alert line), 9+ = red (matches a blocked country in geofencing.geofenced_countries in config.yaml).

spec.title: 🦠 Command & Control (C2) & Intel
spec.description: Section header for the two C2/threat-intel panels below.

options.content: Metrics tracking external C2 and known threat intel hits.

spec.title: Threat Intel IOC Hits (per hour, by feed)
spec.description: Connections that matched a known-bad IP/domain on a threat-intel feed, counted per rolling hour and split by which feed matched. Reputation-based: it catches known-bad infrastructure before Home-IDS's own behavior models would. (Previously plotted the raw counter, which drops to 0 on every restart.)

spec.title: C2 Beacons
spec.description: Count of connections exhibiting Command & Control 'beaconing' — highly uniform, periodic outbound traffic with low jitter (measured via Coefficient of Variation). This is one of the strongest behavioral signals for an active malware infection phoning home, independent of whether the destination has a known-bad reputation yet.

spec.title: 📡 Internal Network Scanning & Probes
spec.description: Section header for the internal recon/scanning panels below.

options.content: Lateral movement, honeypots, and port scans.

spec.title: Lateral Movement Events (per hour)
spec.description: Zeek-detected S0 (unanswered) / REJ (rejected) TCP connection attempts against multiple internal hosts — the classic signature of a device scanning your LAN for other vulnerable machines. This is almost always a sign a device is already compromised and looking for its next target.

spec.title: Honeypot Probes (per hour)
spec.description: Connection attempts to your configured honeypot IP(s) (network_and_devices.honeypot_ips in config.yaml). Only meaningful if you've actually deployed a decoy listener there (see INSTALL.md Step 3.6) — but if you have, ANY hit here is a near-certain compromise signal, since nothing legitimate on your network should ever contact a honeypot.

spec.title: 🔒 Encryption & TLS Anomalies
spec.description: Section header for TLS fingerprinting panels below.

spec.title: Malicious JA3 Hits
spec.description: Same concept as JA4+ (panel to the right) but for the older JA3 fingerprint format — some malware families and older C2 frameworks are only catalogued under JA3.

spec.title: 🌍 How Geofencing Works Here
spec.description: Explains the geofencing_countries default, how to tune it live, and the #1 reason this map can appear empty even when it shouldn't.

options.content:
**How geofencing works.** `geofencing.geofencing_countries` in `config.yaml` currently defaults to blocking `RU`, `KP`, `IR` — any connection whose GeoIP-resolved country matches this list gets an instant CRITICAL verdict, same severity as a confirmed malicious IOC. This is **blocklist-only** (there's no allowlist mode) and it's a `[LIVE]` setting — edit the list in `config.yaml` and it takes effect within seconds, no restart.

**Why the map might look empty:** geofencing (and this whole map) depends entirely on `paths.geoip_db` loading successfully at startup. If it fails to load, the engine logs one line and silently disables GeoIP features — geofencing will never fire and this map will show nothing, even with real traffic. Check your startup logs first before assuming your network is quiet.

spec.title: 🗺️ Top Risky Countries (GeoIP)
spec.description: The same home_ids_geo_risk data as the map above, as a sortable table — useful when you want exact numbers rather than reading map marker sizes. topk(10, ...) shows your 10 highest-risk countries by connection volume/severity. Same gating as the map: every row here already crossed alert_threshold=6.0 to have a value at all -- there's no 'low risk' row, only 'not on this list yet'.

spec.title: 🧬 DGA Signature Combo: Entropy + C2 Beaconing
spec.description: Two independent DGA/botnet signals plotted together so you can see them correlate: Shannon entropy of queried domain names (home_ids_entropy_avg — per ENGINEERING_MANUAL.md, values above ~4.5 mathematically indicate algorithmically-generated, non-human-typed domain names) and C2 beaconing count (home_ids_beaconing_c2_count — periodic, uniform outbound connections). When BOTH lines spike together, that's a strong Domain Generation Algorithm / botnet C2 pattern, much stronger evidence than either signal alone — this is exactly the combination the Hypothesis & Evidence Engine's DGA_BEACONING hypothesis looks for.

spec.title: 🌍 Full Geographic Traffic Context (All Countries, Not Just Risky Ones)
Geographic Traffic Context (All Countries, Not Just Risky Ones)
spec.description: The panels above only surface countries that crossed a risk threshold. This is the full picture -- how much traffic, how many devices, and how much DNS activity your network sends to every country it talks to, risky or not. Useful for spotting 'why does any of my traffic go there at all' even when nothing has been flagged.
